pathway.title: Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, leverage rose in each period. Baldwin's total debt, including the revolver, was USD 1,435.8 million at FY2024, USD 1,710.6 million at FY2025 and USD 2,495.0 million at 2026-06-30, giving total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.59x, 5.01x and 6.30x, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.31x, 4.65x and 5.83x [financial base, leverage chart]. The mechanism is the USD 600.0 million incremental term loan of 2026-01-02 and revolver drawings that rose by USD 195.0 million in six months, set against adjusted EBITDA of USD 396.2 million for the last twelve months that includes about six months of the January 2026 acquisitions. The implication is that the 6.30x probably overstates leverage relative to a full-year pro forma basis by an amount the sources do not size, while the use of company-defined earnings could push the other way, so the ratio is an indicator and not a covenant test.

Second, earnings quality limits every ratio. Adjustments other than interest, amortization and depreciation were 42.5% of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA and 48.6% of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA, and EBITDA before addbacks, calculated from the statements, was USD 58.1 million for the last twelve months against USD 396.2 million adjusted [financial base]. The gap includes USD 128.8 million of Tax Receivable Agreement expense recognized in six months 2026, which the company adds back although the liability is a future cash obligation. The implication is that creditors who underwrite on adjusted EBITDA are relying on management's definition, and the covenant EBITDA may differ.

Third, interest cover held while leverage rose. Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest was 2.81x at FY2024, 2.96x at FY2025 and 2.89x for the last twelve months, but the six-month figure fell from 3.66x to 3.33x as cash interest rose faster than adjusted earnings [financial base]. About USD 500.0 million of the floating-rate term loans is swapped to a fixed 3.244% to 2028-09-14, and a 100 bp rise in SOFR would add USD 14.0 million a year to interest. The implication is that cover is moderate relative to leverage but protected for part of the rate exposure until 2028.

Fourth, liquidity is adequate and narrowing. Cash and equivalents were USD 184.5 million and company-stated undrawn revolver capacity USD 259.4 million at 2026-06-30, against USD 123.7 million and USD 477.0 million at FY2025, with USD 302.0 million drawn on a USD 600.0 million revolver [financial base, liquidity chart]. Fiduciary cash of USD 426.2 million is excluded because it is fiduciary and not free cash. The mechanism is revolver borrowing used alongside USD 126.8 million of share repurchases and acquisition-related payments in six months 2026. The implication is that near-term liquidity covers scheduled amortization of about USD 16.0 million a year, derived, but it is more exposed to cash calls from earnouts and the Tax Receivable Agreement.

Fifth, claims outside debt are large and time-bound. Contingent earnout liabilities were USD 346.8 million at fair value, with undiscounted expected payments of USD 410.5 million of which USD 131.1 million fall within one year, deferred payments were USD 192.5 million undiscounted, and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities were USD 144.6 million at 2026-06-30 [financial base]. The January 2026 acquisitions cost USD 1,559.6 million in total, of which equity was USD 510.6 million and the maximum potential earnout is USD 544.9 million [business and transaction]. The implication is that the true fixed-claim burden exceeds the debt total, and a strong year for the acquired businesses raises earnout payments in cash.

Sixth, control and governance have changed. The Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Court of Chancery on 2026-06-09, the 2024 Stockholders Agreement is in effect, and holders have stated approval rights over debt above 10% of total assets, dividends, large asset transactions and a bankruptcy filing, while the independent committee created in 2024 has been disbanded [business and transaction]. There is no sponsor, and no creditor-adverse transaction is documented. The implication is that leverage and distribution decisions are insider-influenced, and how approvals were applied to the 2025 and 2026 debt additions is not disclosed, so legal capacity cannot be assessed.

Seventh, the business is diversified by client but not by carrier or cycle. The largest client is under 1% of core commissions and fees, while two insurance partners provided about 17%; commissions follow premium levels, organic revenue growth was 2% for six months 2026 against reported growth of 29%, and the Captive adds underwriting exposure of USD 29.5 million of assumed premium earned in six months 2026 [business and transaction]. The implication is that revenue is durable against any single client but exposed to a soft premium market and carrier appetite, and the growth in the period was bought rather than organic.

cells.text: Independent insurance distribution firm with three operating groups: Insurance Advisory Solutions (commercial risk, employee benefits, private risk), Underwriting, Capacity & Technology Solutions (managing general agent platform, reinsurance brokerage, captive) and Mainstreet Insurance Solutions (personal lines, life and health, Medicare through sheltered channels)
Distribution plus manufacturing mixes fee-light brokerage with some risk-bearing, so earnings depend on carrier appetite and premium levels rather than asset values
Commercial property and casualty, employee benefits, personal lines, wealth management and retirement, and Medicare; the industry is described as fragmented and consolidating
Several product lines diversify demand, but each is exposed to premium cycles and, in Medicare, to regulatory compliance

Commission 793,614; profit-sharing 55,645; consulting and service fee 88,356; policy fee and installment fee 41,943; assumed premium earned 29,500; other income 8,592; investment income 7,524; total revenues 1,025,174. Six months 2025: 638,105; 44,300; 47,531; 37,664; 9,805; 9,375; 5,436; total 792,216
Commission is the dominant stream; profit-sharing is a carrier bonus that varies with loss performance, which adds volatility to margin and cash flow

Commissions are generally a percentage of premiums and normally follow premium levels; soft markets put downward pressure, hard markets tend to help; buyers may move to negotiated fees in a hard market
Pricing is set by carriers and the premium cycle, not by Baldwin, so revenue is exposed to a soft market without a direct pricing lever
Medicare contracts are multi-year with renewal commissions; revenue is constrained where reversal risk exists, and the carrier is treated as the customer
Renewal commissions depend on policyholder choices and compliance, which creates reversal risk to cash conversion
Net new business, fees, rate increases, retention, exposure unit growth and contingent commissions; recent partnerships contribute to organic growth only after 12 months of ownership
Acquired revenue is excluded from organic growth for a year, so reported growth overstates underlying momentum in an acquisitive period
Organic revenue growth was 2% for Q2 2026 and 2% for six months 2026, against 11% a year earlier; reported revenue growth for six months 2026 was 29%
The gap between 2% and 29% shows growth is mainly acquired, which raises integration and purchase-price risk
Management cites "normalized organic growth of 8%" for Q2 2026 and sales velocity of 30% in the combined advisory business
Normalized measures are management's definition and are not verified; use the reported organic measure

Largest expense lines for six months 2026: colleague compensation and benefits 547,935, other operating expenses 318,221 (including Tax Receivable Agreement expense of 128.8 million), outside commissions 138,477 and amortization 111,074
A people-heavy cost base is largely fixed in the short run, so a revenue decline in a soft market would compress margin quickly
Capital expenditures were 39,527 in FY2025 and 27,848 in six months 2026
Capital intensity is low relative to earnings, so cash conversion is driven by earnouts, interest and acquisitions rather than capex
Assumed premiums, commissions and fees receivable of 433,617 and fiduciary receivables of 782,194 against fiduciary liabilities of 1,208,383 at 2026-06-30
Fiduciary balances are matched and are not free cash; unrestricted cash is shown separately, so liquidity must exclude fiduciary cash
More than three million clients; largest single client under 1% of core commissions and fees in 2025
Client concentration is low, so single-client loss is not a credit driver
Two insurance company partners accounted for approximately 17% of core commissions and fees in 2025, and one for approximately 10% of commissions and fees
A carrier dispute or appetite change at one or two partners would hit revenue and profit-sharing, which is a concentrated counterparty exposure
About 125 offices in 24 states; the business was historically concentrated in the Southeastern United States and now has several regional concentrations
Regional concentration exposes the book to local catastrophe, loss trends and regulation

The Captive reinsures a quota share of two multifamily programs; assumed premium earned was 29,500 for six months 2026 against 9,805; incurred losses and loss adjustment expense were 14,072 against 8,780; reserve at 2026-06-30 was 23,052
Underwriting exposure is small but growing, and it adds loss volatility and a statutory capital need that the lenders do not control
Large global brokers and private firms are named competitors, including Aon, Marsh & McLennan, Willis Towers Watson, Arthur J. Gallagher, Brown & Brown, Hub International and USI
Scale competitors can outbid for partnerships and talent, which pressures acquisition multiples and retention

runs.text: Strengths. Baldwin's client base is highly diversified, with more than three million clients and no client above 1% of core commissions and fees, so single-client loss is not a credit driver [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Its funded debt is long-dated, with the revolver due 2029-05-24 and the term loans and the 7.125% senior secured notes due in 2031, so refinancing risk is back-ended beyond scheduled amortization [financial base; Analyst Interpretation, because the maturity rows are derived]. Liquidity of USD 184.5 million of cash and USD 259.4 million of undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-06-30 covers near-term scheduled amortization many times over [financial base; Documentary Fact for the inputs]. Cash interest cover on adjusted EBITDA has stayed near 2.9x across three periods, and part of the floating-rate exposure is fixed by a USD 500.0 million swap at 3.244% to 2028-09-14 [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Capital intensity is low, with capital expenditures of USD 39.5 million in FY2025, so cash flow is driven by earnouts, interest and acquisitions rather than reinvestment [financial base; Analyst Interpretation]. Management reports faster integration of CAC Group than planned, but this is Management Language and carries no supporting bridge [business and transaction; Management Language].

Weaknesses. Total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.30x for the last twelve months and net debt to adjusted EBITDA 5.83x, up from 5.01x and 4.65x at FY2025, with the denominator holding only about six months of acquired earnings [financial base; Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]. Adjusted EBITDA relies on addbacks of 48.6% over interest, amortization and depreciation, and the reported result is a net loss of USD 131.8 million for the last twelve months [financial base; Documentary Fact]. All funded debt ranks as first lien and is secured on substantially all assets, so the structure has no subordinated layer beneath the term loans, revolver and notes [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Claims outside debt are material: earnouts of USD 346.8 million, deferred payments of USD 192.5 million and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities of USD 144.6 million [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Operating cash flow after capital expenditures was USD 43.7 million for the last twelve months and negative USD 68.9 million in FY2025, because earnout payments in excess of the accrual run through operations [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Revenue growth is mostly acquired, with organic growth of 2% for six months 2026 [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Control rests with insiders through approval rights over debt, dividends and a bankruptcy filing, with the independent committee disbanded, and Tax Receivable Agreement payments are owed to LLC members [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Two insurance partners provided about 17% of core commissions and fees, and the book was historically concentrated in the Southeast [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. The financial maintenance covenant of 7.00x total first lien net leverage is described only in the FY2025 annual report, with no later reported ratio, so headroom is unmeasured [financial base; Insufficient Information].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The transactions in the pack are a set of completed acquisitions with debt financing, and there is no pending transaction at the cutoff other than a small disposal. Their status is completed unless stated. Source for the terms below is the Q2 2026 10-Q unless a different file is named.

CAC Group (Cobbs Allen Capital Holdings, LLC) was acquired effective 2026-01-01 under a Transaction Agreement dated 2025-12-02 (exhibit 10.32 in the 10-K exhibit list, page:200), amended 2025-12-30. The 10-K describes closing consideration of 438.0 million of cash, 23,200,000 Class A shares and a deferred payment of 70.0 million payable on the fourth anniversary, with contingent consideration payable in cash on post-closing revenue targets (10-K page:188). Obie (Creisoft, Inc.) and Capstone (Foley Insurance Agency, Inc.) were acquired effective 2026-01-02. Obie's consideration was stated as 90.0 million of cash and 396,573 shares plus 122.5 million of deferred payments (10-K page:188). In aggregate the three businesses were recorded at total consideration of 1,559,612 thousand, comprising cash of 567,889, contingent earnouts at fair value of 315,998, equity of 510,561 and deferred payments of 165,164, with goodwill of 1,134,895 and intangible assets of 550,983, and a maximum potential contingent earnout of 544,855 (page:16-19). The purchase accounting is provisional. These businesses contributed total revenues of 202.1 million and a net loss of 42.3 million in six months 2026 (page:17). Management says CAC Group integration is "meaningfully ahead of plan, with approximately 80% of targeted three-year expense synergies already actioned" (Q1 release page:1); that is Management Language and the pack gives no synergy bridge.

Financing and new debt. On 2026-01-02 Amendment No. 4 to the JPM Credit Agreement added 600,000 thousand of incremental term loans on the same terms as the existing Term Loans, with about 12.0 million of debt issuance costs (page:25). No new notes were issued in 2026; the 7.125% Senior Secured Notes due 2031-05-15 remained at 600 million. The company says it intends to fund earnout obligations near term with cash, unused proceeds of the incremental term loans, operating cash flow and revolver borrowings (page:74). The revolver rose from 107,000 thousand to 302,000 thousand over six months 2026, share repurchases were 126,833 thousand, and a 25.0 million deferred payment to a partner was settled on 2026-01-02 (10-K page:189). Use of proceeds therefore combined acquisition funding, earnout and deferred payment settlement and shareholder returns; the pack does not give a sources and uses statement for the add-on, and none is inferred.

Earlier financings, for the timeline: on 2024-05-24 the company issued 600 million of 7.125% Senior Secured Notes and put in place an 840 million first lien term loan and a 600 million revolver (10-K page:161); incremental term loans followed on 2025-01-10 (100.0 million) and 2025-09-18 (75.0 million) (10-K page:164-165).

Disposal. A plan to sell CACH Media Guarantors Insurance Solutions, LLC was committed in Q2 2026 and a definitive agreement for 4.0 million of cash, of which about 2.1 million is in escrow, was signed on 2026-07-02, a subsequent event after the 2026-06-30 balance sheet date (page:46-47). It is immaterial by the company's own assessment.

Share repurchase. On 2026-02-26 the board authorized repurchases of up to 250 million of Class A stock over the following twelve months, with about 124.5 million remaining at 2026-06-30 (page:83; Q4 release page:1).

Creditor read-through. The January 2026 transactions raised debt, equity and non-debt claims together. Leverage mechanics are in the financial base: total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 6.30x for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30, against 5.01x at FY2025, with the limit that the earnings include about six months of acquired businesses. The equity component of consideration, 510,561 at fair value, is not a debt claim but dilutes existing holders. Items outside the pack: the Transaction Agreement, the Amendment No. 4 document, the indenture and the credit agreement, so permitted debt, restricted payments and collateral cannot be tested.

fields.value: The financial base supports a bounded reported-fact view of Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. at the consolidated level, with specific limits. Reported FY2024 and FY2025 statements are audited and consolidated. Six-month 2026 and 2025 statements are unaudited. The base is dominated by the January 2026 acquisitions of CAC Group, Obie and Capstone, which closed against a 600,000 thousand incremental term loan, new equity and new contingent claims. As a result the 2025 comparatives and the FY2025 balance sheet are not like for like with 2026. On the company's adjusted EBITDA definition, total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 4.59x at FY2024, 5.01x at FY2025 and 6.30x on a last-twelve-months basis to 2026-06-30, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 4.31x, 4.65x and 5.83x. Cash interest cover on the same earnings is 2.81x, 2.96x and 2.89x. These ratios are calculated here from printed components and are not company-reported credit metrics. Three limits bind every use. First, adjusted EBITDA carries large management addbacks, and EBITDA before addbacks, calculated from the statements, is far lower, so the leverage view depends on which earnings measure a reader accepts. Second, the last-twelve-months earnings include six months of acquired earnings while the 2026-06-30 debt carries the full acquisition financing, and a pro forma adjusted EBITDA for the 2026 acquisitions is not supplied, so the 6.30x is probably overstated relative to a full-year acquired run rate by an amount the pack does not size. Risk mechanism: the acquisition debt is fully in the numerator while only six months of acquired earnings is in the denominator, and management addbacks are a large share of the earnings, so the ratio can move materially with the covenant definition. Creditor implication: the first lien covenant at 7.00x (10-K page:164) cannot be tested from the pack, and the adjusted figure should not be read as covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest burden. Evidence: net interest expense of 144,698 for the last twelve months and cash interest cover of 2.89x. Risk mechanism: the Term Loans and revolver are floating, with a 500,000 swap to a fixed 3.244% covering part of the exposure, and the notes at 7.125% pay semi-annually, so quarterly cover is seasonal (2.10x in Q2 2025 and 2.33x in Q2 2026, both quarters containing the May coupon). Creditor implication: the six-month trend in cover fell from 3.66x to 3.33x as interest rose faster than adjusted earnings; the 100 bp sensitivity is 14.0 million a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity. Evidence: cash of 184.5 million and undrawn capacity of 259.4 million at 2026-06-30, against 123.7 million and 477.0 million at 2025-12-31. Risk mechanism: revolver drawings rose by a net 195,000 in six months while cash paid for repurchases and acquisition-related payments was large. Creditor implication: liquidity remains sizeable against near-term scheduled debt service, but the buffer fell and sits ahead of a 2029 revolver maturity and 346,824 of earnout liabilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Claims outside debt. Evidence: earnouts of 346,824, deferred payments of 192,500 undiscounted and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities of 144,570. Risk mechanism: these are contractual or probable cash outflows that compete with debt service, and the earnouts are at fair value with a maximum for the 2026 deals of 544,855. Creditor implication: debt-only leverage understates fixed and contingent cash claims; downstream work must show them separately.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion. Evidence: net cash from operations of 39,486 for six months 2026 and an outflow of 80,704 for six months 2025, with earnout payments in excess of the accrual of 6,739 and 85,090. Risk mechanism: most of the swing is lower earnout payments and no colleague earnout incentive payments inside operating cash flow (31,824 in 6M 2025), so cash flow before earnouts is a better indicator of conversion. Creditor implication: adjusted free cash flow of 46,225 is the company's definition and adds back earnout payments; it should not be mistaken for free cash flow after all acquisition-related payments.

fields.value: - Comparability. Evidence: acquired businesses added revenue of 202.1 million in six months 2026 while organic revenue growth was 2% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:17, page:60). It distributes commercial property and casualty, employee benefits, personal lines, wealth and retirement, and Medicare products through three operating groups, and manufactures proprietary insurance products through its managing general agent platform. The credit story of the period is a step change in scale and leverage. Three partnerships, led by CAC Group, closed on 2026-01-01 and 2026-01-02 for total consideration of 1,559,612 thousand, financed through a mix of 600,000 thousand of incremental term loans under Amendment No. 4, Class A shares issued to sellers, contingent earnouts and deferred payments, while cash and revolver borrowing also rose over the period. Control rights instead rest with the pre-IPO members of the operating company, who hold Class B shares and, under a stockholders agreement that the Delaware Supreme Court reinstated on 2026-06-09, approval rights over mergers, large asset deals, borrowing above stated thresholds, equity issuance and dividends. Revenue is recurring in form, since it is commissions, fees and carrier bonuses on renewing policies, but it follows premium levels and carrier relationships, and the reported growth for the first half of 2026 is mostly acquired. The facts that matter most to a creditor are the acquisition-related cash claims outside debt, the insider approval rights and the absence of a supplied credit agreement, so permitted debt, restricted payments and guarantor perimeter cannot be tested here. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. has an elevated-leverage but adequately liquid credit profile, and this synthesis holds that view with Medium confidence. Its strongest support is a diversified, commission-based client base, first-lien debt with no maturity before the revolver on 2029-05-24 beyond scheduled amortization, and USD 184.5 million of cash plus USD 259.4 million of undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-06-30. The weakest point is leverage: total debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 6.30x for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30 from 5.01x at FY2025, on earnings that rely on large addbacks and hold only six months of the January 2026 acquisitions. Whether acquired earnings reach run rate, whether earnout and deferred payments are met without new borrowing, and covenant headroom, which is not supplied, decide the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, leverage rose in each period. Baldwin's total debt, including the revolver, was USD 1,435.8 million at FY2024, USD 1,710.6 million at FY2025 and USD 2,495.0 million at 2026-06-30, giving total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.59x, 5.01x and 6.30x, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.31x, 4.65x and 5.83x [financial base, leverage chart]. The mechanism is the USD 600.0 million incremental term loan of 2026-01-02 and revolver drawings that rose by USD 195.0 million in six months, set against adjusted EBITDA of USD 396.2 million for the last twelve months that includes about six months of the January 2026 acquisitions. The implication is that the 6.30x probably overstates leverage relative to a full-year pro forma basis by an amount the sources do not size, while the use of company-defined earnings could push the other way, so the ratio is an indicator and not a covenant test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, earnings quality limits every ratio. Adjustments other than interest, amortization and depreciation were 42.5% of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA and 48.6% of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA, and EBITDA before addbacks, calculated from the statements, was USD 58.1 million for the last twelve months against USD 396.2 million adjusted [financial base]. The gap includes USD 128.8 million of Tax Receivable Agreement expense recognized in six months 2026, which the company adds back although the liability is a future cash obligation. The implication is that creditors who underwrite on adjusted EBITDA are relying on management's definition, and the covenant EBITDA may differ.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, interest cover held while leverage rose. Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest was 2.81x at FY2024, 2.96x at FY2025 and 2.89x for the last twelve months, but the six-month figure fell from 3.66x to 3.33x as cash interest rose faster than adjusted earnings [financial base]. About USD 500.0 million of the floating-rate term loans is swapped to a fixed 3.244% to 2028-09-14, and a 100 bp rise in SOFR would add USD 14.0 million a year to interest. The implication is that cover is moderate relative to leverage but protected for part of the rate exposure until 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, liquidity is adequate and narrowing. Cash and equivalents were USD 184.5 million and company-stated undrawn revolver capacity USD 259.4 million at 2026-06-30, against USD 123.7 million and USD 477.0 million at FY2025, with USD 302.0 million drawn on a USD 600.0 million revolver [financial base, liquidity chart]. Fiduciary cash of USD 426.2 million is excluded because it is fiduciary and not free cash. The mechanism is revolver borrowing used alongside USD 126.8 million of share repurchases and acquisition-related payments in six months 2026. The implication is that near-term liquidity covers scheduled amortization of about USD 16.0 million a year, derived, but it is more exposed to cash calls from earnouts and the Tax Receivable Agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, claims outside debt are large and time-bound. Contingent earnout liabilities were USD 346.8 million at fair value, with undiscounted expected payments of USD 410.5 million of which USD 131.1 million fall within one year, deferred payments were USD 192.5 million undiscounted, and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities were USD 144.6 million at 2026-06-30 [financial base]. The January 2026 acquisitions cost USD 1,559.6 million in total, of which equity was USD 510.6 million and the maximum potential earnout is USD 544.9 million [business and transaction]. The implication is that the true fixed-claim burden exceeds the debt total, and a strong year for the acquired businesses raises earnout payments in cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, control and governance have changed. The Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Court of Chancery on 2026-06-09, the 2024 Stockholders Agreement is in effect, and holders have stated approval rights over debt above 10% of total assets, dividends, large asset transactions and a bankruptcy filing, while the independent committee created in 2024 has been disbanded [business and transaction]. There is no sponsor, and no creditor-adverse transaction is documented. The implication is that leverage and distribution decisions are insider-influenced, and how approvals were applied to the 2025 and 2026 debt additions is not disclosed, so legal capacity cannot be assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seventh, the business is diversified by client but not by carrier or cycle. The largest client is under 1% of core commissions and fees, while two insurance partners provided about 17%; commissions follow premium levels, organic revenue growth was 2% for six months 2026 against reported growth of 29%, and the Captive adds underwriting exposure of USD 29.5 million of assumed premium earned in six months 2026 [business and transaction]. The implication is that revenue is durable against any single client but exposed to a soft premium market and carrier appetite, and the growth in the period was bought rather than organic.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Baldwin's client base is highly diversified, with more than three million clients and no client above 1% of core commissions and fees, so single-client loss is not a credit driver [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Its funded debt is long-dated, with the revolver due 2029-05-24 and the term loans and the 7.125% senior secured notes due in 2031, so refinancing risk is back-ended beyond scheduled amortization [financial base; Analyst Interpretation, because the maturity rows are derived]. Liquidity of USD 184.5 million of cash and USD 259.4 million of undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-06-30 covers near-term scheduled amortization many times over [financial base; Documentary Fact for the inputs]. Cash interest cover on adjusted EBITDA has stayed near 2.9x across three periods, and part of the floating-rate exposure is fixed by a USD 500.0 million swap at 3.244% to 2028-09-14 [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Capital intensity is low, with capital expenditures of USD 39.5 million in FY2025, so cash flow is driven by earnouts, interest and acquisitions rather than reinvestment [financial base; Analyst Interpretation]. Management reports faster integration of CAC Group than planned, but this is Management Language and carries no supporting bridge [business and transaction; Management Language].

fields.name: Quote

Total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.30x for the last twelve months and net debt to adjusted EBITDA 5.83x, up from 5.01x and 4.65x at FY2025, with the denominator holding only about six months of acquired earnings [financial base; Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]. Adjusted EBITDA relies on addbacks of 48.6% over interest, amortization and depreciation, and the reported result is a net loss of USD 131.8 million for the last twelve months [financial base; Documentary Fact]. All funded debt ranks as first lien and is secured on substantially all assets, so the structure has no subordinated layer beneath the term loans, revolver and notes [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Claims outside debt are material: earnouts of USD 346.8 million, deferred payments of USD 192.5 million and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities of USD 144.6 million [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Operating cash flow after capital expenditures was USD 43.7 million for the last twelve months and negative USD 68.9 million in FY2025, because earnout payments in excess of the accrual run through operations [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Revenue growth is mostly acquired, with organic growth of 2% for six months 2026 [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Control rests with insiders through approval rights over debt, dividends and a bankruptcy filing, with the independent committee disbanded, and Tax Receivable Agreement payments are owed to LLC members [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Two insurance partners provided about 17% of core commissions and fees, and the book was historically concentrated in the Southeast [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. The financial maintenance covenant of 7.00x total first lien net leverage is described only in the FY2025 annual report, with no later reported ratio, so headroom is unmeasured [financial base; Insufficient Information].
